tasks.subject: Task 2: Membership, invites, admin rules and drives
tasks.description:
**Goal:** `src/members.ts` decides who gets in and enforces every admin rule from the spec, as plain functions over the database.

**Files:**
- Create: `apps/server/src/members.ts`, `apps/server/tests/members.test.ts`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] First sign-in by `ADMIN_EMAIL` into an empty member list creates an admin.
- [ ] A live invite for the signed-in email creates the member with the invite's role, marks the invite used, and clears `removed_at` for a re-invited removed member.
- [ ] No invite while sign-ups are `invite` gives `not-invited` with reason `none`; a token that is expired, used, cancelled, or for another email gives that reason and the inviter's name.
- [ ] Sign-ups `open` creates a member without an invite.
- [ ] A removed member gets `removed`.
- [ ] Non-admins are refused every admin action; nobody changes or removes themselves; the last admin cannot be demoted or removed.
- [ ] Invite tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes; inviting an existing member is refused.
- [ ] A member can add and remove only their own drives.

**Verify:** `cd apps/server && node --test` → `# fail 0`

Full steps and code: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-23-accounts.md, Task 2: Membership, invites, admin rules and drives.

tasks.subject: Task 3: Offline pass (server signs, web verifies)
tasks.description:

- Modify: `apps/web/package.json` (add `test:account`, add it to `test`)

**Acceptance Criteria:**

tasks.subject: Task 4: Identity adapter
tasks.description:
**Goal:** `whoIs(request)` is the only code that decides who a request is: TinyAuth headers only from the edge on the gated site, or a verified TinyAuth OIDC ID token as a bearer, or a fixed dev identity on localhost.

**Files:**
- Create: `apps/server/src/identity.ts`, `apps/server/tests/identity.test.ts`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Headers are accepted only when the socket address is the configured edge address AND `X-Cave-Gate: tinyauth` is present (Caddy sets it on the gated site only).
- [ ] The same headers from any other address are ignored (null).
- [ ] A bearer RS256 or EdDSA JWT is accepted only with the right issuer, audience, unexpired `exp`, and an `email` claim; any one wrong gives null.
- [ ] `DEV_IDENTITY` is used only for requests from 127.0.0.1 / ::1, and only when set.

**Verify:** `cd apps/server && node --test` → `# fail 0`

Full steps and code: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-23-accounts.md, Task 4: Identity adapter.

tasks.subject: Task 6: HTTP API, static files, and start-up
tasks.description:
**Goal:** A running server: `/api/*` routes over Tasks 2-5, the built web app with the cache rules, and settings read from the environment.

**Files:**
- Create: `apps/server/src/static.ts`, `apps/server/src/api.ts`, `apps/server/src/main.ts`, `apps/server/tests/api.test.ts`, `apps/server/.env.example`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `GET /api/me` answers `{ status: 'member', member, drives, firstVisit, pass }` for a member, `{ status: 'not-invited', ... }`, `{ status: 'removed', ... }`, or 401 `{ error: 'signed-out' }` with no identity. It reads the invite token from `X-Cave-Signup`.
- [ ] `PATCH /api/me` changes name/colour/welcomed; `POST /api/me/drives` and `DELETE /api/me/drives/:id` work for the member's own drives.
- [ ] Every `/api/admin/*` route answers 403 `{ error: 'not-admin' }` for a member; rule errors answer 409 with the code (`self`, `last-admin`, `already-member`); `not-found` answers 404.
- [ ] `POST /api/admin/invites` answers `{ invite, link, emailed }`; the link is `PUBLIC_URL/?signup=<token>`.
- [ ] Static: `/` and unknown paths give `index.html` with `Cache-Control: no-store`; `/assets/x.js` gives `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`; `..` paths are refused.
- [ ] Cross-origin requests from the desktop app's origins (`tauri://localhost`, `http://tauri.localhost`) get CORS headers allowing `Authorization`, `Content-Type`, `X-Cave-Signup`; other origins get none.

**Verify:** `cd apps/server && node --test` → `# fail 0`

tasks.subject: Task 7: Web account client and state
tasks.description:
**Goal:** The web app knows who is signed in: a pure API client (tested against the real server code in-process), and `account.svelte.ts` that starts the account, keeps the offline pass, and feeds the live-session name and colour.

**Files:**
- Create: `apps/web/src/lib/account-api.ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/account.svelte.ts`
- Modify: `apps/web/tests/account.check.ts`, `apps/web/vite.config.ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/sync.svelte.ts:18` (export `COLORS`)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `me()` returns `{ kind: 'member', ... }`, `{ kind: 'not-invited', ... }`, `{ kind: 'removed' }`, `{ kind: 'signed-out' }` for 401 or a redirect, and `{ kind: 'offline' }` when fetch throws.
- [ ] Requests use `redirect: 'manual'` and `credentials: 'include'`, add `Authorization: Bearer` when a token getter returns one, and `X-Cave-Signup` when a sign-up token is given.

**Verify:** `cd apps/web && npm run test:account` → `account: all ok`; `npm run check` → no new errors

tasks.subject: Task 11: Desktop sign-in
tasks.description:
**Goal:** The desktop app signs in through TinyAuth's OIDC provider (system browser, PKCE, `cavecad://auth` back) and calls the API with a bearer ID token; the server does the code exchange so the webview needs no CORS from TinyAuth.

**Files:**
- Modify: `apps/web/src/lib/desktop-signin.ts` (replace the stub), `apps/server/src/desktop-token.ts` (replace the stub), `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs` (add `open_url`), `apps/web/src/lib/desktop.ts` (add `openUrlNative`), `apps/web/src/lib/account.svelte.ts` (desktop path), `apps/web/src/components/account/AccountGate.svelte` (desktop Sign in), `apps/web/src/App.svelte` (route `cavecad://auth` links)
- Test: `apps/web/tests/account.check.ts`, `apps/server/tests/desktop-token.test.ts`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `pkcePair()` gives a 43+ character verifier and its S256 challenge (checked against a known RFC 7636 example).
- [ ] `authorizeUrl()` includes `response_type=code`, `client_id`, `redirect_uri=cavecad://auth`, `scope=openid email profile`, `code_challenge`, `code_challenge_method=S256`, and `state`.
- [ ] `readAuthLink()` accepts `cavecad://auth?code=…&state=…` only when `state` matches.
- [ ] The server's `/api/desktop-token` posts `grant_type=authorization_code` (or `refresh_token`) with the client secret to TinyAuth's token endpoint and returns `{ id_token, refresh_token, expires_in }`; TinyAuth errors come back as 400 `{ error: 'sign-in-failed' }`.
- [ ] In the desktop app, the gate's Sign in opens the system browser; the returning link signs in and `startAccount()` runs with the bearer.

**Verify:** `cd apps/server && node --test` → `# fail 0`; `cd apps/web && npm run test:account` → `account: all ok`; the real round trip is checked by Nathan after deployment (Task 13).

tasks.subject: Task 13: Deployment files and the go-live checklist
tasks.description:
**Goal:** Everything needed to put accounts on `cave.schonegg.stream`, written down and checked: the server's service file, the Caddy site block (with the header wipe), the TinyAuth additions, and a check script; then deployed with Nathan approving each server change.

**Files:**
- Create: `deploy/README.md`, `deploy/cavecad-server.service`, `deploy/Caddyfile.cave`, `deploy/tinyauth-additions.md`, `deploy/check-edge.sh`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `deploy/Caddyfile.cave` removes `Remote-User`, `Remote-Email`, `Remote-Name`, `Remote-Groups`, `Remote-Sub` and `X-Cave-Gate` from incoming requests before `forward_auth`, sets `X-Cave-Gate: tinyauth` itself, and has a second site `cave-api.schonegg.stream` for the desktop app with no `forward_auth` and the same header wipe.
- [ ] `deploy/check-edge.sh` fails if a request with a forged `Remote-Email` and a browser User-Agent reaches the app instead of the TinyAuth login, or if `cave-api.` answers anything but 401 without a bearer.
- [ ] The README lists the steps in order, starting with the server inventory, and marks each step that changes the server as needing Nathan's go-ahead.
- [ ] After deployment: `deploy/check-edge.sh` passes, and Nathan has signed in with Google, sent himself an invite, opened it with a second account, and opened the app in airplane mode.

**Verify:** `bash -n deploy/check-edge.sh` → no output; after deployment `bash deploy/check-edge.sh` → `edge: all ok`
